record.paper_title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
record.original_question: If disk-like Einstein-Vlasov configurations are surrounded by dark-matter-halo-like matter distributions, does this improve convergence of the numerical algorithm and support the existence of realistic flattened disk-galaxy morphologies in the Einstein-Vlasov system?

evidence.quote: A different aspect is that it is often claimed that halos of dark matter may be crucial to the pronounced flattened shape of disk galaxies.

It is a question of great importance to investigate if such halos surrounding disk-like solutions do improve the convergence of the numerical algorithm. If this turns out to be the case, it would give significant support to the established claim that disk galaxies are embedded in dark matter halos. To our knowledge this has not been investigated for the Einstein-Vlasov system and we find it to be an essential open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the axially symmetric Einstein–Vlasov system in general relativity, which describes a collisionless ensemble of particles whose phase-space distribution function f on the cotangent bundle of spacetime is constant along geodesics of a metric g, while g satisfies the Einstein equations with stress-energy tensor

  T^{μν}(x) = ∫ f(x,p) p^μ p^ν (dp / √(−det g)),

the integration being over the mass shell {p : g^{μν}(x) p_μ p_ν = −m^2, p^0 > 0}. Restrict to stationary, axially symmetric solutions: there exist commuting Killing fields ∂_t and ∂_φ, and one looks for distribution functions of the form f = Φ(E, L_z), where E = −p_t and L_z = p_φ are the conserved energy and angular momentum per unit mass.

A "disk-like configuration" is a stationary axisymmetric solution whose matter support is highly flattened toward the equatorial plane z = 0. Standard iterative numerical schemes (of fixed-point type, alternately solving the metric field equations from a given matter distribution and updating the matter distribution by integrating Φ(E, L_z) against the new metric) are known to converge well for spherical and moderately flattened configurations but to suffer convergence problems as the matter support becomes increasingly disk-like.

A "dark-matter halo" component is an additional Vlasov matter component, supported on a region surrounding (and extending well beyond) the disk-like component, prescribed by an ansatz Φ_halo(E, L_z) chosen so that its spatial support is approximately spheroidal and its total mass is comparable to or larger than that of the disk component.

Problem. Determine whether augmenting a disk-like axisymmetric Einstein–Vlasov configuration with such a surrounding Vlasov "dark-matter halo" component improves the convergence of the standard iterative numerical algorithm for stationary axially symmetric solutions, and whether this leads to the existence (and explicit construction) of stationary solutions of the Einstein–Vlasov system whose matter distribution exhibits a realistic flattened disk-galaxy morphology embedded in an extended halo.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up any work investigating whether surrounding disk-like axisymmetric Einstein–Vlasov configurations with halo-like Vlasov matter improves convergence of the iterative numerical scheme or yields flattened disk-galaxy stationary solutions. Existing literature on the Einstein–Vlasov system addresses spherically symmetric and moderately flattened axisymmetric stationary solutions and convergence of related schemes, but not this specific halo-augmentation question, which appears to remain unaddressed.

status_evidence.title: The Einstein–Vlasov System/Kinetic Theory (Living Reviews)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of stationary solutions of the Einstein–Vlasov system, including axially symmetric configurations; no construction of disk-galaxy solutions with embedded Vlasov halos is reported.
status_evidence.claim: Standard surveys do not record a solution to the halo-embedded disk-like Einstein–Vlasov problem.

status_evidence.title: The Einstein-Vlasov System/Kinetic Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Review of numerical and analytical results for stationary axially symmetric Einstein–Vlasov configurations; difficulties in obtaining strongly flattened disk-like solutions are noted.
status_evidence.claim: Flattened disk-galaxy stationary solutions remain a recognized difficulty.
